item.text: {"case_id":"SPR00143","decision":"candidate","candidate_ranking":["C22","C06","C02"],"selected_candidate_label":"C22","confidence":0.98,"relationship_type":"both","rationale":"C22 is a compelling reusable template because it is an earlier enlargement of the same monument and supplies both the proclamation machinery and concrete survey material reused in the child. Both recite acquisition of adjoining land for monument protection or administration, invoke section 2 of the 1906 act, incorporate acquired land into Muir Woods, provide a metes-and-bounds description, and give the same warning. More distinctively, the child's survey repeats several exact bearings and distances appearing in C22, including the consecutive 143.10-foot and 491.22-foot courses, showing direct reuse of the earlier boundary description rather than merely common monument boilerplate. C06 and C02 are strong structural analogues for contemporaneous monument enlargements but lack C22's same-monument and exact-survey overlap.","shared_material":[{"child_excerpt":"under and by virtue of the authority vested in me by section 2 of the act of June 8, 1906, 34 Stat. 225 (16 U.S.C. 431)","parent_excerpt":"under and by virtue of the authority vested in me by section 2 of the act of June 8, 1906, 34 Stat. 225 (16 U.S.C. 431)","explanation":"Identical statutory authority and proclamation formula within the same monument-enlargement context."},{"child_excerpt":"north 38°05' east 143.10 feet ... north 8°12'30\" west 491.22 feet","parent_excerpt":"S 28° 05' W., 143.10 ft.; S. 8° 12' 30\" E., 491.22 ft.","explanation":"The same consecutive distances and closely corresponding boundary bearings appear in reverse-direction survey courses, strongly indicating reuse of the earlier Muir Woods boundary description."},{"child_excerpt":"the following-described lands, in California, are hereby added to and reserved as a part of the Muir Woods National Monument","parent_excerpt":"the lands within the following-described boundaries which are now owned or controlled by the United States shall constitute the Muir Woods National Monument","explanation":"Both use acquired or controlled adjoining lands and a legal description to enlarge the same monument."},{"child_excerpt":"Warning is hereby expressly given to all unauthorized persons not to appropriate, injure, destroy, or remove any features of this monument and not to locate or settle upon any of the lands thereof.","parent_excerpt":"Warning is hereby expressly given to all unauthorized persons not to appropriate, injure, destroy, or remove any feature of this monument and not to locate or settle upon any of the lands thereof.","explanation":"Nearly verbatim warning language reinforces the direct textual continuity."}]}
